title: What a card shows while you play it
summary: A card in play is presented rather than simply shown: the game keeps an icon-only front, its own stat icons and a damage display, so what you read off a card is put there deliberately.
body: A card is presented, not just displayed. The game ships an icon-only version of a card front, which is what a card looks like when it is being shown rather than handled.
There are stat icons for a card. The game keeps its own icons for things a card can have, covering a critical, a boss, a fist and a defence among them, so what a card is capable of is drawn on it.
Damage is shown separately. There is an element damage display of its own, which is why a card's element matters visibly during play and not only in the rules.

Cards are drawn in a queue. The game keeps a draw queue with its own states covering the hand, the discard, the centre and the top or bottom of a deck, which is why moving a card is tracked rather than instant.
Effects are their own data. Card effects are kept as their own records, so what a card does in play is defined rather than hard-coded into the card.

The damage display is drawn from lists. It carries a background colour and a power text, and it keeps a list of element background colours beside a list of element icons, so a card's element is a colour and a symbol rather than a word.

It is placed rather than fixed. The display has a position offset and a rotation offset and it can follow the card's rotation, which is why the same damage readout sits properly whether the card is in a hand or lying on a table.
Cards also have display settings. The game keeps settings for how a card is shown, which is why the same card can be presented differently in a hand and on a board.

The elements have pictures of their own. The game ships an icon per element for a card in play, a red-and-yellow flame for fire, a blue wave for water, a green rock for earth and a yellow swirl for wind among them, which is what the damage display's list of element icons points at.
What this entry does not tell you: what any icon means in rules terms, how much damage anything does, or how many effects exist. We have not verified those, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: The game ships an icon-only card front for presenting a card.
There are stat icons for things a card can have, including a critical, a boss, a fist and a defence.
Element damage is shown by a display of its own.
Cards move through a draw queue with named destinations.
Card effects are kept as their own records.
Cards have display settings of their own.
The element damage display carries a background colour and a power text, with a list of element background colours and a list of element icons.
It has a position offset and a rotation offset, and it can follow the card's rotation.
The game ships its own element icons for a card in play, including icons for fire, water, earth and wind.
facts.evidence: asset names: Icon_Fire, Icon_Water, Icon_Earth, Icon_Wind
